scope: Read-only independent original-image, source, package-byte and wire-record review. No rerun, recapture, model/clock write, production change or original-report edit.
attemptAttribution: ARM native/occupied-port/Rosetta were executed in attempt 2; Intel was executed in attempt 1 and retained byte-for-byte. Actual report timestamps below are preserved; refreshed GitHub check IDs are not new executions.

packageBytes.scope: Whole ZIP/DMG files, all declared ZIP app members and actual executable bytes independently rehashed here. DMG mount/install/signature execution is supported by original macOS receipts, not rerun on this Linux reviewer.

Original SDK and complete identity card
Real gameplay actions and START pause/resume

visualObservations: All six original screenshots viewed individually: actual ship, weapon, teammates and gameplay HUD rendered.

Continue and Quit are fully visible, without the identity card covering them.
Disconnected capture removes the client card; reconnect restores the same full ID while retaining the paused scene and timer.
Menu heading and narrative wrap in the narrow left column; lower instruction lines require internal scrolling. The large Start action remains visible.

visualObservations: Four original captures show identical loading-failed shader-precision errors.
Only a static controller-panel heading appears: no rendered client icon/ID or actual world.
The three-frame lost-context/null-precision probe and actual app error support limited_graphics only; no Intel gameplay or rendered-card pass is claimed.

limits: No physical ESP32 controller, consumer Mac or television was tested. The unchanged original Python SDK drives the actual AppKit/WKWebView app on CI runners.
Rosetta x86_64 graphics on Apple GPU does not establish Intel Mac graphics compatibility. Intel remains strict limited_graphics/webgl_incomplete: protocol/lifecycle/error screen only.
Native CF observes movement, turn, fire, pitch aim and START transitions. Reload/jump are only labelled input-consumed in the native suite; browser mechanics acceptance retains its separate scope.
No complete native CF round or end-of-round screen is claimed.

At the captured 1024-pixel width the menu title wraps and lower controller instructions extend beyond the initial scroll viewport. Start, complete controller ID and pause actions remain visible. Not all instructions fit without scrolling.

The original Intel game snapshot has webglError=false while stage=error and the exact getShaderPrecisionFormat null error are present. This review preserves that flag and uses the actual error plus the independent three-frame lost-context probe; it does not turn the flag into true.
Package receipts describe ad-hoc signing and no Apple notarization.
